body.html:
Spec-1 fleet primer · two rounds · decontaminated proof

The fleet primer, proven and priced: real information, one lost law, and what caching does to the math

86 agents · 2 rounds · round-1 control contaminated → redesigned · PRIMED 6/7 vs control 4/7 · the caching caveat stated honestly

What was tested
Spec-1's claim: a 4,064-token optical primer of the full 18-file doc tier (bp context pack, 5.35× vs 21.7k raw) makes a worker as law-correct as reading the raw docs, and both beat an unprimed control. Round 1's control was contaminated — the harness injects CLAUDE.md into every subagent, so 'no-docs' workers aced router-law scenarios (9.8!). Round 2 was redesigned: seven laws verified to live ONLY in cards/contracts, control forbidden from docs. All workers Opus 4.8, judged against card-verified keys.

Round-2 scoreboard (decontaminated)

ArmMeanLaw-correctWhat it proves
SELFREAD (raw docs)9.87/7the accuracy ceiling
PRIMED (optical)8.66/7near-parity — the whole gap is ONE cell
HARNESS-DEFAULT5.84/7the primer carries real doc-only information
• The control gap is real and diagnostic. The no-docs arm failed exactly the doc-fiat laws: safe workspace delete (honest refusal), PATH FROZEN (inverted), and the plugin law — where it confidently answered the EXACT forbidden pattern (route around the host). Where it scored high, the source was code, world knowledge, or ambient memory — never the docs it lacked.
• The optical channel dropped one of seven laws. The terse one-line fiat 'docs/cli/** is PATH FROZEN' (cli.md:11) did not survive into the primed worker's answer — it reasoned from the generic doc contract to a harmful inverted verdict. Everything else transmitted at full fidelity, including exact code anchors (bcp47_to_iso6392b/1, @default_retry_delays_ms, assertStripComplete). Excluding that cell: 9.7 vs 9.8, and PRIMED beat SELFREAD once (the raw-text arm misread Elixir arity notation as an attempt count).
• Round-1 side finding: workers already carry the router CLAUDE.md ambiently — a primer's incremental value is the 16 cards/contracts beyond it.

The economics, stated honestly

Raw math: ~11–16k input tokens saved per worker, ~110–480k per 10–30-worker wave. But prompt caching largely erases this: identical prepended context re-reads at ~0.1× after the first worker, so cached-raw vs cached-primer differ by ~1.3k token-equivalents per worker — and raw docs is the accuracy winner. What keeps the primer alive: (a) self-read as workers actually do it (each independently grepping) is NOT cross-worker cacheable and costs tool-turns and latency; (b) the primer occupies 4k vs 17.5k of each worker's finite window; (c) at corpus scale the calculus flips — the 238-paper KB is 849k as text (uncacheable headroom-wise) vs 131k packed.

Ruling and the resulting doctrine

PARTIAL — transmission is real but not lossless
The primer provably transmits doc-only law (control gap), at near-parity fidelity — but it dropped one terse fiat rule out of seven, producing a harmful inverted answer. Doctrine: for the standard fleet wave, prepend the RAW tier and let caching pay for it — accuracy wins and the cost argument is moot. Deploy the optical primer where the window, not the bill, is the constraint (huge corpora, long-running workers needing headroom), and pair it with a laws-index sidecar: the tier's one-line fiat rules extracted as text riding alongside the pages — exactly the mechanism that already protects exact strings, extended to terse laws.
